question: ‘The Unforgettables’ was the collection of semi-classical music of which Ghazal singer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jagjit Singh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Unforgettables:-**

 
 
• **The collection of semi-classical music "The Unforgettables" was by the Ghazal singer Jagjit Singh and his wife Chitra Singh.**
 
• The album was released in two volumes in 1976 and 1978, respectively.
 
• It features a selection of their most popular ghazals, as well as some lesser-known gems. The album is considered to be a classic of Indian music and has been reissued numerous times.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jagjit Singh:-**

 
 
• **He is often referred to as the "Ghazal King".**
 
• He was a renowned Indian composer, singer, and musician who played a pivotal role in revitalizing and popularizing the ghazal, an ancient form of Urdu poetry set to music.
 
• Born in Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, on February 8, 1941, Singh's melodious voice and heartfelt renditions captivated audiences worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Mehdi Hassan:-**
 
 
• **He is a British-American broadcaster and best-selling author of Indian descent.**
 
• He has presented The Mehdi Hasan Show on Peacock since October 2020 and on MSNBC since February 2021.
 
• Hasan is known for his progressive and critical views on politics, media, and society.
 
• He has been praised for his sharp wit and incisive commentary, but he has also been criticized for his sometimes abrasive style.
 
 
 
• **Mallika Pukhraj:-**
 
 
• **She was a highly popular ghazal and folk singer of Pakistan. **
 
• She was generally known as "Malika", meaning "The Queen", publicly. She was extremely popular for her rendition of Hafeez Jalandhri's nazm song, Abhi tau main jawan hoon ("I am still young"), which is enjoyed by millions not only in Pakistan, but also in India. 
 
 
 
• **Talat Mahmood:-**
 
 
• **He was an Indian playback singer and a ghazal maestro. He was born in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, to a family with a rich musical heritage. **
 
• Talat's melodious voice and emotive renditions of ghazals made him one of the most sought-after singers of the Golden Era of Hindi cinema.
 
• He lent his voice to legendary actors like Dilip Kumar, Dev Anand, Raj Kapoor, and Sunil Dutt, and sang some of the most memorable Hindi film songs of the 1940s, 1950s, and 1960s.
